cells.tense: The fire for the direction is lit, and you are here with it, choosing with the pen in hand.
cells.ask: Sketch the next three moves for the thing you're lit up about, in order, then do only the first this week. Let the other two sit.
cells.core:
There's a fire lit for a direction, and you're standing in it, choosing with your hand on the pen. The confidence isn't loud; it's usable. People feel it when you say what you're for, and that's how things start. Going well, the plan serves the spark instead of replacing it — you pick a line and mean it, and the whole want stays intact while you move.

What bends it now is how easy it is to keep the fire broad. Choosing a direction means dropping the others, and you haven't felt that cost yet. So the work: sketch the next three moves for the thing you're lit up about, in order, then do only the first this week. Let the other two sit. You'll have a direction with a step under it, and the spark won't have to hold the whole map.
cells.sheetLine: The spark is real. Choose the next step, not the whole map.
cells.verb: starting something before you know where it's going, and letting the confidence carry you into choosing
cells.place: the part of you that says this, not that, and means it

cells.tense: The direction is racing ahead of the person, bracing at a future that can't be written in.
cells.act: ask the question you do not know the answer to
cells.ask: Pick an area you're pushing forward and ask it something you honestly can't answer. Stay with the answer before deciding anything else.
cells.core:
The fire has gotten ahead of you. You're directing before the direction has arrived — starting things fast enough that speed outruns whether they're true, and confidence is doing work the facts should be doing. From outside it looks like certainty. From inside it's bracing, because a future you can't write in is exactly what you're pushing against.

What's missing is the opposite motion: listening, discerning, letting something land without argument. So the work: pick an area you're pushing forward and ask it something you honestly can't answer. Stay with the answer before deciding anything else. That's all. The fire doesn't go out — it starts coming from what you found out, not from what you were sure of.

cells.tense: The spark already went somewhere behind a door, and you are still at that door.
cells.act: tend the small thing and learn from it
cells.ask: Find something you've meant to begin and spend ten minutes with your hands on it, no plan past that. Let it show you what it needs.
cells.core:
There was a fire, and it's behind you. You're at the door of something you meant to start, and the direction you'd have chosen isn't in your hands now. The spark hasn't gone — it just isn't moving. Chances to begin again come toward you and don't land, and you keep the readiness without the step.

What's starved here charges through the small and material: tending something, learning how it grows. So the work: find something you've meant to begin and spend ten minutes with your hands on it, no plan past that. Let it show you what it needs. You don't push energy into the starved spot. You put your hands on something living and the current comes back through.

cells.tense: You are already directing the direction, and the one holding the line doesn't sign the page.
cells.act: lay the one step you can see, solidly
cells.ask: Name the next step you can already see in what you're steering, put it on paper, and set it down solid this week. Nothing after it.
cells.core:
You're steering. The direction is being chosen — by you — and the one doing it doesn't call it choosing. Asked, you might say the thing started itself, the group was already moving that way, it's obvious where it's headed. The line between what you began and what you merely went along with is drawn by your hand, and you don't count it as yours.

What returns it is the simpler form of the same act: building one solid thing, without claiming the whole structure. So the work: name the next step you can already see in what you're steering, put it on paper, and set it down solid this week. Nothing after it. The step is yours on paper, which is what acknowledgment is — the author standing beside the page.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that the person's radiance is 'already matured' and pulling others along; the record supports a learning energy that explores and starts things, not a proven track record, so the cells describe the spark and its present bend rather than a history. The reader could object that confidence is not what's happening and that what looks like shining is performance; each Too Much and Too Little cell is written so that reading still works. The ask survives being wrong because it is one small act of the medicine, useful whether or not the read is true, and it never makes anything depend on the person agreeing with the picture. The sentence that serves the writer more than the person is the balanced sheet line about the spark being usable as is, so it was narrowed to name what choosing one direction costs when the others drop.
